chunks: Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام:

I inform you, my master, that your servant ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār instructed in his will that hajj be performed on his behalf from an estate, a quarter of which he assigned for you: one hajj every year with twenty dinars. But since the route to al-Baṣrah was cut off, the expense upon the people has multiplied, so they are no longer content with twenty dinars. Likewise, a number of your followers made bequests concerning two hajj pilgrimages.
So he عليه السلام wrote: “Three hajj pilgrimages are to be made into two, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest in his will
key_terms.الْمَئُونَةُ: the expense or cost of provision and travel
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a dinar, used here as the financial amount allocated
key_terms.ضَيْعَةٍ: an estate or landed property producing income
key_terms.يُحَجَّ: that hajj be performed on someone's behalf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bequest for hajj becomes insufficient because travel expenses increase?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a bequest for hajj on behalf of a deceased person when the allocated funds became insufficient due to increased travel costs. The Imam عليه السلام gives a practical legal ruling: the originally intended number of pilgrimages may be reduced proportionally so that the bequest remains workable.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2928 - Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar wrote to Abu Muhammad (as):

"I inform you, my master, that your servant Ali ibn Mahziyar instructed in his will that Hajj be performed on his behalf from a property, a quarter of which he dedicated for this purpose, allocating one Hajj every year with twenty dinars. However, since the route to Basra has been cut off, the expenses for travel have significantly increased, and twenty dinars are no longer sufficient. Similarly, several of your followers have made wills for two Hajj pilgrimages."
Imam (as) wrote back: "Combine three Hajj pilgrimages into two, God willing."
